newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn falters to new lows on Midwest weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn falters to new lows on Midwest weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower and a set of contract lows were notched in the nearby five months with nearly ideal crop weather in the U.S. Midwest weighing on values, traders said.
"We continue to make new lows. There's very, very good weather and nothing exciting on the old crop side," said Tom Levis, Prudential Securities grain analyst.
Warm weather plus showers and high humidity further enhanced crop production prospects, the traders said.
Rainfall was again reported overnight in key U.S. corn growing states and crop condition ratings will likely show another improvement when weekly reports are issued next Monday, sources said.
Late Monday this week, USDA said the crop was 67 percent good to excellent as of Sunday, up slightly from the 66 percent in that category the previous week.
The new contract low for July is $2.55-3/4 per bushel, below the previous low of $2.58-1/2 set Tuesday. The new low for new crop December is $2.40-1/4, below the previous low of $2.41-3/4 set Monday.
Corn closed unchanged to five cents lower, with July down four at $2.56-1/4. December was down five at $2.40-3/4.

Dry weather in portions of China's grain growing region and a private forecast this week for potentially dry weather in the U.S. Midwest by late next week may have limited declines, some traders said.

LFG Futures sold ten million bushels of December while Merrill Lynch Futures and Dean Witter each sold four million December, traders said. Term Commodities bought 7.5 million bushels of December and Cargill Inc bought eight million bushels of July, traders said.

In spread trading, Smith Barney did 2.5 million July/December at 15 cents, premium July, Continental Grain spead 1.5 million December/July at 15 cents, premium July and Farmers Commodities Corp did 1.5 million September/July at 13 cents, premium July, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 85,000 contracts, below the 82,055 traded Tuesday.

In corn options, Farmers Commodities Corp sold 500 September $2.60 calls at 4-3/4 to five cents, LIT America bought 500 December $2.60 calls at 7-1/2 cents, sold 500 December $2.90 calls at 3-1/2 cents and sold 500 December $2.20 puts at three cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, slightly above the 12,957 traded Tuesday.
